  There is no greeting, no handshake, no "come in" sweep of the arm, no warmth
  of any kind.
- **He keeps his hat on the whole time he is at the door** — he only takes it
  off once he is over the threshold (≈298.5 s). By the manners of the period
  that marks the visit as official business rather than a social call, which is
  exactly the kind of caller she is treating him as.
- **The camera has already told us to distrust him.** Before she ever opens up
  we get those seconds of him alone in a shadowed hall with his silhouette
  looming on the door — the shot is lit and composed for menace.
- **Even after she lets him in she does not relax.** She follows him into the
  living room a step behind and stays half-screened behind his shoulder
  (≈299.3–302.6 s) rather than leading him in or showing him to a seat.

The one thing pulling the other way is small: in the last second or two before
she admits him (≈296.4–297.5 s) her head tilts, she speaks more freely and her
expression softens to something close to a faint, polite half-smile. But that
comes *after* the doorstep interrogation, and it is politeness, not trust. The
overall reading is unmistakable: she is guarded, controlled and suspicious, and
she opens up only because he has given her a reason to.

## How her reaction changes once she is standing between the two men

When the older man in the pale suit walks in and pulls off his white panama, the
three of them settle into a single sustained three-shot: he is on her left, the
caller is on her right, both of them in the foreground turned towards each
other, and she is set back in the middle between them while they talk to *each
other* across her. Her contained wariness gives way to open alarm and
helplessness. What shows it:

- **Her eyes fly wide open.** From about 307 s the whites are visible around her
  irises — a fixed, startled stare that never once appeared during the doorway
  scene.
- **Her eyebrows lift and her mouth drops open.** Her lips part and stay parted
  as she listens (≈307.7–309 s), and at ≈310–311 s her mouth opens further, as
  if she has caught her breath or blurted something out.
- **Her gaze darts back and forth between the two men.** Her head stays almost
  still while her eyes flick left to the man with the panama and then right to
  the caller, following the exchange passing over her head. At the door her gaze
  had been fixed and steady on one man; here it is unsettled and shuttling.
- **Her posture goes rigid and passive.** She stands stiffly upright with her
  arms hanging at her sides. At the door she had a hand on the door and was the
  one deciding who came in; now she is holding nothing and deciding nothing.
- **The blocking traps her.** The two men are framed large in the foreground on
  either side of her, while she is recessed in the middle distance and made to
  look smaller between them — literally boxed in. She has gone from guarding her
  own threshold to being penned in her own living room.
- **She falls silent and simply reacts.** At the door she was the one asking the
  questions; in the three-shot the men speak past her and the camera holds on
  her face, so the whole weight of the scene lands on her expression — which is
  dismay.

## In short

At the door she does **not** look trusting: she cracks the door, peers round it,
keeps her hand on it and her body in the gap, never smiles, and keeps a hatted
stranger standing out in the hall for the best part of ten seconds before
grudgingly letting him in. A minute later, standing between the two men while
they talk over her, that composure is gone: she is wide-eyed, open-mouthed,
stiff-armed and silent, her eyes flicking from one man to the other — wariness
has turned into visible alarm at something she can no longer control.

# Answer

## Where this happens in the video

The first time a man is seen waiting outside an apartment door is at roughly 4:45 to 4:48 (about 285–288 s). A man in a dark fedora and overcoat stands in a dim hallway in front of a numbered apartment door (the number reads as 34), his shadow thrown large across the door while he waits. At about 4:48 (288 s) the door swings open and a blonde woman in a light floral dress opens it for him. (The opening credits show only a silhouette at the Norths' door with nobody answering, so this hallway scene is the first real instance.)

## Does she look trusting of him? Yes.

She looks trusting, relaxed, and even pleased to see him, not guarded. The evidence is in her body language and face:

1. **She opens the door wide and stands in the open doorway.** She does not crack the door, peer through a gap, keep a hand on the door to close it, or stay behind it. She stands squarely in the doorway facing him with her body fully exposed to him.

2. **Her first reaction is a lively greeting gesture, not alarm.** The moment she sees him (about 288.3–289 s) she throws a hand up to shoulder height, palm out, with her mouth open and eyebrows raised as if saying "Oh, hello!" It reads as surprised, happy recognition of someone she knows, not fear.

3. **She chats with him casually for about ten seconds.** From about 289 to 298 s she stands with one hand resting on her hip, weight settled, face turned up to him, talking and listening in an easy, unhurried way. She never glances back into the apartment or checks over her shoulder.

4. **She smiles and tilts her head at him.** Around 296.5–298 s she cocks her head to one side and breaks into a broad smile, almost a laugh; the pose is flirtatious and completely at ease.

5. **She lets him straight in.** At about 298–300 s he takes off his hat and walks across the threshold, and she simply steps back out of his way to admit him. She then follows him into the living room behind him, walking at his back with no sign of keeping distance.

Everything about the door exchange says she knows this man and has no fear of him.

## How her reaction changes when she stands between the two men

Once inside (about 301–305 s) a second man, tall, in a light suit with a white hat, appears from the far side of the living room with his hat still on and takes it off as he joins them. From about 306 s the three of them stand in a line: the light-suited man on the left, the woman in the middle, and the dark-suited visitor on the right. The two men face each other and talk across her. Her manner changes from warm and open to uneasy and wary. What shows this:

1. **The smile disappears.** In the three-shot (306–328 s) her face is set and serious. Her eyebrows lift slightly and her lips stay closed or barely parted; there is none of the laughing, head-tilting playfulness she showed at the door.

2. **She goes quiet and turns into a spectator.** The men do the talking while she stands between them watching; her mouth stays mostly closed and she appears to say very little, whereas at the door she had been talking animatedly with her hands moving.

3. **Her posture closes up.** Instead of the loose hand-on-hip stance, she stands stiffly with her arms bent and her hands held in close at her waist, planted between the two men without moving.

4. **Her eyes dart back and forth between the two men.** In the three-shot, and even more clearly in the tight close-up on her face (about 328–338 s), her gaze swings to the left toward the light-suited man, then to the right toward the visitor, then back again, tracking every exchange. Her brow is drawn and her mouth slightly open; she looks anxious about where the conversation is going.

5. **Her hand goes to her throat.** At about 337 s she raises her hand and presses it to her throat and collarbone, a classic self-protective, nervous gesture, while her eyes drop and half close. She then gives a sidelong glance to the side, turns her head away from both men (about 338.5–339.5 s), and withdraws to sit down on the sofa (about 340 s), leaving the men standing over her.

## Summary

At the door she is trusting: she opens up fully, greets him with a raised hand, chats with a hand on her hip, smiles and tilts her head, and steps aside to let him walk in. Caught between the two men in the living room she becomes tense and apprehensive: her smile vanishes, she falls silent and stands rigid with her hands drawn in, her eyes flick nervously from one man to the other, and finally she clutches her throat, looks away, and retreats to the sofa.
